features.name: mean_reply_word_count
features.definition: What is the mean number of words per counter-argument comment?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings. Word count of a comment = len(re.findall(r"\S+", comment)). Return the mean of word counts across all comments. Empty list -> null; missing or malformed JSON -> null. Raw text count with no semantic filtering; text may include outcome announcements.

features.name: mean_reply_word_count_squared
features.definition: What is the square of the mean number of words per counter-argument comment?
features.spec: df['mean_reply_word_count'] ** 2; null if df['mean_reply_word_count'] is null.

h0: The coefficient on mean_reply_word_count_squared is zero (no accelerating or decelerating effect of reply length on delta, controlling for mean_reply_word_count).
h1: The coefficient on mean_reply_word_count_squared is positive (reply length has a super-linear, accelerating association with delta).
note: Operational assumptions: reply length is measured as mean word count across all supplied counter-argument comments per row (no per-comment outcomes supplied, so row-level mean is used; one long comment among many short ones is diluted). Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change). A quadratic term tests super-linearity; it is a functional-form proxy for 'disproportionate benefit for very long replies' and does not specifically isolate the extreme tail. The OLS is a linear probability model. Associations only, not causal. Comment text may contain outcome announcements and the list order carries no chronology; log_length is not used because its construction is undocumented.
